critical_code_review_comments: LeadForm phone sanitization strips +91 and leading 0 correctly via cleanPhone regex; validation is applied to the raw value AND the submit button uses validPhone(f.phone) on every render — good UX.
Duplicate blocking on backend (server.py line ~452) matches on exact stored phone; sanitized 10-digit form is stored, so duplicate detection works consistently.
Admin force-create logs a duplicate_log entry — good for audit trail.
Contact panel WhatsApp link builds waPhone = '91' + 10 digits — correct; also copes with pre-sanitized numbers.

Minor UX: on the LeadDetail contact-panel, the copy-phone and copy-email buttons rely on navigator.clipboard.writeText which may fail silently in browsers without clipboard permission (e.g. non-secure contexts, some in-app webviews). Consider a fallback to document.execCommand('copy') or at least a toast.error on catch(). Currently the .then() only fires on success. Non-blocking.
Non-blocking: Recharts 'width(-1)/height(-1)' warnings on dashboard are cosmetic (hidden chart containers during first paint).

seed_data_creation: Created two new leads during testing: IR07007 (sales, phone 9876543210) and IR07008 (admin force-created duplicate of same phone). These can be left as-is or cleaned up by main agent if desired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All phone-validation, duplicate-blocking, admin-override, contact-panel and quick-action flows are verified end-to-end. Two duplicate leads (IR07007 & IR07008) both hold phone 9876543210, so any further duplicate testing on that phone will now consistently trigger the dialog. Note: browser automation must call `context.grant_permissions(['clipboard-read','clipboard-write'])` before testing copy-phone / copy-email toasts, otherwise the writeText promise rejects and the toast never fires (this is a Playwright sandbox quirk, not an app bug).
